To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the WAIS- IV/WMS- IV Adult battery can be interpreted in terms of a general ability factor or a model that does not include a general ability factor.

two measurement models fit the data well: (a) a seven-factor model with no general ability factor (Verbal Comprehension Index, Perceptual Index, Working Memory Index, Processing Speed Index, Auditory Memory Index, Visual Memory Index) and (b) a five-factor model with a hierarchical general factor (Verbal, Perceptual, Working Memory, Processing Speed, Memory).

the WAIS- IV/WMS-IV battery has two factor structures that are equally supported by the data, and that the factor structure of the combined WAIS-IV and WMS-IV tests is different from the factor structure of either the WAIS-III/WMS-III battery or the WAIS- III/WMS-R battery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a factor structure that best represents the data and provides clinicians with the most useful information for the interpretation of WAIS-IV and WMS-IV scores.
the factor structure of WAIS-IV and WMS-IV.
the factor structure of the WAIS/WMS battery and its implications for interpretation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the WAIS- IV/WMS-IV battery can be used to measure seven independent factors or five independent factors plus a general factor of intelligence.
the WAIS-III/WMS-III Adult battery factor structure has been replicated in the WAIS- IV/WMS-IV battery.
the WAIS- IV/WMS-IV co-norming is a valuable and useful battery of tests.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the WAIS- IV/WMS-IV battery can be used as two separate batteries or as a combined test battery.
the factor structure of the WAIS/WMS battery can be conceptualized in a number of ways, and that a general factor is not necessary to explain the relationship among the subtest scores.
the seven-factor model without the hierarchical factor is the most appropriate model for WAIS-IV and WMS-IV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the WAIS- IV and WMS-IV are two separate tests and should not be combined into a single battery of tests.
there is no single best factor structure for the WAIS- IV/WMS-IV combined battery.
clinicians can use the WAIS-4/WMS-4 battery as a combined test battery and still interpret the results of the individual tests.
